blocks.title: Theorem
blocks.html:
Theorem 2.1

Let \( k \) be a perfect field of characteristic \( p>0 \), \( S=\Spec(k) \), \( \overline{S}=\Spec(W_2(k)) \) (1.3), and let \( X \) be a smooth \( S \)-scheme. To every smooth \( \overline{S} \)-scheme \( \widetilde{X} \) lifting \( X \) is canonically associated an isomorphism \[ \varphi_{\widetilde{X}} : \bigoplus_{i<p} \Omega^i_{X'/S}[-i] \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } \tau_{<p} F_* \Omega^{\bullet}_{X/S} \] of \( D(X') \), such that \( \mathscr{H}^i \varphi_{\widetilde{X}} = C^{-1} \) (1.2) for \( i<p \).

The proof will be carried out in four steps.

Proof▾

(a) Reduction to the definition of \( \varphi^1_{\widetilde{X}} \). The datum of \( \varphi_{\widetilde{X}} \) is equivalent to the datum, for \( i<p \), of an arrow \( \varphi^i_{\widetilde{X}} : \Omega^i_{X'/S}[-i] \to F_* \Omega^{\bullet}_{X/S} \) in \( D(X') \) such that \( \mathscr{H}^i \varphi^i_{\widetilde{X}} = C^{-1} \). The arrow \( \varphi^0_{\widetilde{X}} \) is necessarily the composite \[ \mathcal{O}_{X'} \xrightarrow{\ C^{-1}\ } \mathscr{H}^0 F_* \Omega^{\bullet}_{X/S} \to F_* \Omega^{\bullet}_{X/S}. \] Suppose \( \varphi^1_{\widetilde{X}} \) defined such that \( \mathscr{H}^1 \varphi^1_{\widetilde{X}} = C^{-1} \). For \( i \geqslant 1 \), consider the product map

\[ (\Omega^1_{X'/S})^{\otimes i} \to \Omega^i_{X'/S}, \qquad \omega_1 \otimes \ldots \otimes \omega_i \mapsto \omega_1 \wedge \ldots \wedge \omega_i ; \]

for \( i<p \), this admits the "antisymmetrization" section \( a \), given by \[ a(\omega_1 \wedge \ldots \wedge \omega_i) = (1/i!) \sum_{s \in \mathfrak{S}_i} \sgn(s)\, \omega_{s(1)} \otimes \ldots \otimes \omega_{s(i)} . \]

For \( 1 \leqslant i<p \), let us define \( \varphi^i_{\widetilde{X}} \) as the composite arrow \[ \xymatrix{ (\Omega^1_{X'/S})^{\otimes i}[-i] \ar[rr]^-{(\varphi^1_{\widetilde{X}})^{\otimes i}} & & (F_* \Omega^{\bullet}_{X/S})^{\otimes i} \ar[d]^-{\text{produit}} \\ \Omega^i_{X'/S}[-i] \ar[u]^-{a[-i]} \ar[rr]_-{\varphi^i_{\widetilde{X}}} & & F_* \Omega^{\bullet}_{X/S} . } \]

It follows from the multiplicative property of the Cartier isomorphism that \( \mathscr{H}^i \varphi^i_{\widetilde{X}} = C^{-1} \), and \( \varphi_{\widetilde{X}} = \sum_{i<p} \varphi^i_{\widetilde{X}} \), with \( \varphi^0_{\widetilde{X}} \) as above, answers the question. It therefore suffices to define \( \varphi^1_{\widetilde{X}} : \Omega^1_{X'/S}[-1] \to F_* \Omega^{\bullet}_{X/S} \) such that \( \mathscr{H}^1 \varphi^1_{\widetilde{X}} = C^{-1} \), which we will do in the following three steps.

(b) Case where \( F: X \to X' \) lifts. Let \( \widetilde{X}' \) be the \( S \)-scheme deduced from \( \widetilde{X} \) by the base change \( \sigma : \overline{S} \to \overline{S} \) (1.3). Suppose given a \( \overline{S} \)-morphism \( \widetilde{F} : \widetilde{X} \to \widetilde{X}' \) lifting \( F \). Since \( F^* : \Omega^1_{X'/S} \to F_* \Omega^1_{X/S} \) is zero, the image of \( \widetilde{F}^* : \Omega^1_{\widetilde{X}'/S} \to \widetilde{F}_* \Omega^1_{\widetilde{X}/S} \) is contained in \( p \widetilde{F}_* \Omega^1_{\widetilde{X}/S} \). Since multiplication by \( p \) induces an isomorphism \( p : F_* \Omega^1_{X/S} \xrightarrow{\sim} p \widetilde{F}_* \Omega^1_{\widetilde{X}/S} \), there therefore exists a unique arrow \[ f = p^{-1} \widetilde{F}^* : \Omega^1_{X'/S} \to F_* \Omega^1_{X/S} \] making the square \[ \xymatrix{ \Omega^1_{\widetilde{X}'/S} \ar[r]^-{\widetilde{F}^*} \ar[d] & p \widetilde{F}_* \Omega^1_{\widetilde{X}/S} \\ \Omega^1_{X'/S} \ar[r]_-{f} & F_* \Omega^1_{X/S} . \ar[u]_-{\simeq | p} } \] commute.

If \( x \) is a local section of \( \mathcal{O}_{\widetilde{X}} \), with reduction \( x_0 \bmod p \), one has

\[ \tag{1} \widetilde{F}^*(x \otimes 1) = x^p + p\, u(x) \]

with \( u(x) \) a section of \( \mathcal{O}_{\widetilde{X}} \) (and \( p : \mathcal{O}_X \xrightarrow{\sim} p \mathcal{O}_{\widetilde{X}} = \) multiplication by \( p \)), and

\[ \tag{2} f(dx_0 \otimes 1) = x_0^{p-1} dx_0 + d\,u(x) . \]

In particular, one has

\[ \tag{3} df = 0 , \]

so that \( f \) defines a morphism of complexes \[ f : \Omega^1_{X'/S}[-1] \to F_* \Omega^{\bullet}_{X/S} , \] such that \( \mathscr{H}^1 f = C^{-1} \) by (2).

(c) Homotopies. Let, for \( i=1, 2 \), \( \widetilde{F}_i : \widetilde{X} \to \widetilde{X}' \) be a \( \overline{S} \)-morphism lifting \( F \). Then \( \widetilde{F}_2^* - \widetilde{F}_1^* : \mathcal{O}_{\widetilde{X}'} \to p \widetilde{F}_* \mathcal{O}_{\widetilde{X}} = p F_* \mathcal{O}_X \) is a derivation, which determines a \( \mathcal{O}_{X'} \)-linear map \[ h_{12} : \Omega^1_{X'/S} \to F_* \mathcal{O}_X \] making the diagram \[ \xymatrix{ \mathcal{O}_{X'} \ar[r]^-{\widetilde{F}_2^* - \widetilde{F}_1^*} \ar[d] & p \widetilde{F}_* \mathcal{O}_{\widetilde{X}} \\ \mathcal{O}_{X'} \ar[d]_-{d} & \\ \Omega^1_{X'/S} \ar[r]_-{h_{12}} & F_* \mathcal{O}_X . \ar[uu]_-{\simeq | p} } \] commute.

If, for \( x \) as in (b), \( \widetilde{F}_i^*(x \otimes 1) = x^p + p\, u_i(x) \), then \[ h_{12}(dx_0 \otimes 1) = u_2(x) - u_1(x) , \] whence, taking (2) into account,

\[ \tag{4} f_2 - f_1 = d\, h_{12} , \]

where \( f_i = p^{-1} \widetilde{F}_i^* : \Omega^1_{X'/S} \to F_* \Omega^1_{X/S} \).

If, for \( i=1, 2, 3 \), \( \widetilde{F}_i : \widetilde{X} \to \widetilde{X}' \) is a \( S \)-morphism lifting \( F \), and \( h_{ij} \) corresponds to \( \widetilde{F}_j - \widetilde{F}_i \), then one has

\[ \tag{5} h_{12} + h_{23} = h_{13} . \]

(d) General case. Since \( X/S \) is smooth, \( F \) admits, locally for the Zariski topology on \( X \), a lifting \( \widetilde{F} \) [(SGA 1 III)] or (EGA IV § 17)]. One can therefore find an open covering \( \mathscr{U}=(U_i)_{i \in I} \) of \( X \), and, for each \( i \), a \( S \)-morphism \( \widetilde{F}_i : \widetilde{U}_i \to \widetilde{U}'_i \) lifting \( F \) (\( X, X', \widetilde{X}, \widetilde{X}' \) have the same underlying spaces; one denotes by \( \mathscr{U}', \widetilde{\mathscr{U}}, \widetilde{\mathscr{U}}' \) the open coverings of \( X', \widetilde{X}, \widetilde{X}' \) deduced from \( \mathscr{U} \)). Let, as in (b) and (c), \[ f_i = p^{-1} \widetilde{F}_i^* : \Omega^1_{X'/S} | U'_i \to F_* \Omega^1_{X/S} , \] and, on \( U'_{ij} = U'_i \cap U'_j \), \( h_{ij} : \Omega^1_{X'/S} | U'_{ij} \to F_* \Omega^1_{U_{ij}/S} \) corresponding to \( \widetilde{F}_j^* - \widetilde{F}_i^* \). One has

\[ \tag{6} df_i = 0 , \qquad f_j - f_i = d\, h_{ij} \ (\text{sur } U'_{ij}) , \qquad h_{ij} + h_{jk} = h_{ik} \ (\text{sur } U'_{ijk} = U'_i \cap U'_j \cap U'_k) . \]

Let \( \check{\mathscr{C}}(\mathscr{U}, \Omega^{\bullet}_{X/S}) \) be the simple complex associated with the Čech double complex of \( \Omega^{\bullet}_{X/S} \), defined as follows. Set \( \Delta_n = \{0, \ldots, n\} \), and, for \( s : \Delta_n \to I \), denote by \( U_s \) the intersection of the \( U_{s(n)} \) and \( j_s \) the inclusion of \( U_s \) in \( X \). The component of degree \( n \) of \( \check{\mathscr{C}}(\mathscr{U}, \Omega^{\bullet}_{X/S}) \) is \[ \check{\mathscr{C}}(\mathscr{U}, \Omega^{\bullet}_{X/S})^n = \bigoplus_{a+b=n} \check{\mathscr{C}}^b(\mathscr{U}, \Omega^a_{X/S}) , \] where \( \check{\mathscr{C}}^b(\mathscr{U}, \Omega^a_{X/S}) \) is the product, extended over the \( s : \Delta_b \to I \), of the \( j_{s*} j_s^* \Omega^a_{X/S} \). The differential of \( \check{\mathscr{C}}(\mathscr{U}, \Omega^{\bullet}_{X/S}) \) is \( d = d_1 + d_2 \), with \( d_1 : \check{\mathscr{C}}^b(\mathscr{U}, \Omega^a_{X/S}) \to \check{\mathscr{C}}^b(\mathscr{U}, \Omega^{a+1}_{X/S}) \) induced by the differential of the de Rham complex, and \( d_2 : \check{\mathscr{C}}^b(\mathscr{U}, \Omega^a_{X/S}) \to \check{\mathscr{C}}^{b+1}(\mathscr{U}, \Omega^a_{X/S}) \) equal to \( (-1)^a \sum (-1)^i \partial_i \). The obvious morphisms \( \Omega^a_{X/S} \to \check{\mathscr{C}}^0(\mathscr{U}, \Omega^a_{X/S}) \) define a quasi-isomorphism \( \Omega^{\bullet}_{X/S} \to \check{\mathscr{C}}(\mathscr{U}, \Omega^{\bullet}_{X/S}) \), and consequently a quasi-isomorphism

\[ \tag{7} F_* \Omega^{\bullet}_{X/S} \to F_* \check{\mathscr{C}}(\mathscr{U}, \Omega^{\bullet}_{X/S}) . \]

Let us define \[ \varphi^1_{(\mathscr{U}, (\widetilde{F}_i))} = (\varphi_1, \varphi_2) : \Omega^1_{X'/S} \to F_* \check{\mathscr{C}}(\mathscr{U}, \Omega^{\bullet}_{X/S})^1 = F_* \check{\mathscr{C}}^1(\mathscr{U}, \mathcal{O}_X) \oplus F_* \check{\mathscr{C}}^0(\mathscr{U}, \Omega^1_{X/S}) \] by \[ (\varphi_1 \omega)(i,j) = h_{ij}[\omega | U'_{ij}] , \qquad (\varphi_2 \omega)(i) = f_i[\omega | U'_i] . \]

The relations (6) express that \( d \varphi^1_{(\mathscr{U}, (\widetilde{F}_i))} = 0 \), i.e. that \( \varphi^1_{(\mathscr{U}, (\widetilde{F}_i))} \) is a morphism of complexes

\[ \tag{8} \varphi^1_{(\mathscr{U}, (\widetilde{F}_i))} : \Omega^1_{X'/S}[-1] \to F_* \check{\mathscr{C}}(\mathscr{U}, \Omega^{\bullet}_{X/S}) . \]

Finally, let us define

\[ \tag{9} \varphi^1_{\widetilde{X}} : \Omega^1_{X'/S}[-1] \to F_* \Omega^{\bullet}_{X/S} \]

as the arrow of \( D(X') \) composed of (8) and the inverse of (7). Let us check that (9) does not depend on the choice of \( (\mathscr{U}, (\widetilde{F}_i)) \). It is clear that (9) does not change if one replaces \( \mathscr{U} \) by a finer covering, the \( \widetilde{F}_i \) by the induced liftings. If \( (\mathscr{U}=(U_i)_{i \in I}, (\widetilde{F}_i)_{i \in I}) \) and \( (\mathscr{V}=(V_i)_{i \in J}, (\widetilde{F}_i)_{i \in J}) \) are two choices, the coverings \( \mathscr{U} \) and \( \mathscr{V} \) are finer than \( \mathscr{U} \coprod \mathscr{V} \), indexed by \( I \coprod J \), and \( (\mathscr{U}, (\widetilde{F}_i)_{i \in I}) \) and \( (\mathscr{V}, (\widetilde{F}_i)_{i \in J}) \) define the same arrow (9) as \( (\mathscr{U} \coprod \mathscr{V}, (\widetilde{F}_i)_{i \in I \coprod J}) \).

It then only remains to show that \( \mathscr{H}^1 \varphi^1_{\widetilde{X}} = C^{-1} \). This is a local question, so one may assume that \( F \) admits a lifting \( \widetilde{F} : \widetilde{X} \to \widetilde{X}' \). The arrow \( \varphi^1_{\widetilde{X}} \) is then defined by the morphism of complexes \( f \) of (b), and we saw that \( \mathscr{H}^1 f = C^{-1} \). This completes the proof of 2.1.

blocks.title: Remarks
blocks.html:
Remarks 2.2

(i) One has not really used the hypothesis that \( S \) is the spectrum of a perfect field: the proof in fact provides an isomorphism \( \varphi_{\widetilde{X}} \) for \( S \) equal to the reduction modulo \( p \) of a scheme \( \overline{S} \) flat over \( \mathbf{Z}/p^2 \) equipped with an endomorphism \( F_{\overline{S}} \) lifting \( F_S \) (\( \widetilde{X}' \) is then defined as deduced from \( \widetilde{X} \) by the base change \( F_{\overline{S}} \)). We will study later (3.7) the dependence of \( \varphi^1_{\widetilde{X}} \) on \( \widetilde{X} \).

(ii) In the case where \( F : X \to X' \) admits a lifting \( \widetilde{F} : \widetilde{X} \to \widetilde{X}' \), the arrow \( f = p^{-1} \widetilde{F}^* \) of (b) above extends to a quasi-isomorphism of complexes of \( \mathcal{O}_{X'} \)-modules

\[ \tag{2.2.1} \varphi_{(\widetilde{X}, \widetilde{F})} : \bigoplus_{i \geqslant 0} \Omega^i_{X'/S}[-i] \to F_* \Omega^{\bullet}_{X/S} \]

inducing \( C^{-1} \) on \( \mathscr{H}^i \) (and such that \( \tau_{<p} \varphi_{(\widetilde{X}, \widetilde{F})} \) has image \( \varphi_{\widetilde{X}} \) in \( D(X') \)): it indeed suffices to define the component of degree \( i \) of \( \varphi_{(\widetilde{X}, \widetilde{F})} \), \[ \varphi^i_{(\widetilde{X}, \widetilde{F})} : \Omega^i_{X'/S} \to Z F_* \Omega^i_{X/S} \] as \( C^{-1} \) for \( i=0 \), and, for \( i \geqslant 1 \), as the composite of \( \Lambda^i f : \Omega^i_{X'/S} \to \Lambda^i Z F_* \Omega^1_{X/S} \) and the product \( \Lambda^i Z F_* \Omega^1_{X/S} \to Z F_* \Omega^i_{X/S} \) (\( Z \) denoting the kernel of \( d \)).

(iii) The local liftings of \( F \) form a torsor on \( X' \) under the sheaf \( \sHom(\Omega^1_{X'/S}, F_* \mathcal{O}_X) = \Theta_{X'/S} \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_{X'}} F_* \mathcal{O}_X \) of derivations of \( X' \) with values in \( F_* \mathcal{O} \). The class \( c \) of this torsor in \( H^1(X', \Theta_{X'/S} \otimes F_* \mathcal{O}_X) \) is the obstruction to the existence of a global lifting \( \widetilde{F} : \widetilde{X} \to \widetilde{X}' \) of \( F \). With the notation of (d) above, and up to a sign depending on the chosen conventions, \( c \) is the class of the cocycle \( (h_{ij}) \). By the very construction of \( \varphi^1_{\widetilde{X}} \), the class \( c \), regarded as an arrow from \( \Omega^1_{X'/S}[-1] \) to \( F_* \mathcal{O} \) in \( D(X') \), is none other than the composite of \( \varphi^1_{\widetilde{X}} \) and the natural projection \( F_* \Omega^{\bullet}_{X/S} \to F_* \mathcal{O}_X \); the obstruction to representing \( \varphi^1_{\widetilde{X}} \) by a morphism of complexes.

(iv) Suppose that \( X \) admits a smooth formal lifting \( X^{\wedge} \) over \( W(k) \), and let \( m \) be an integer \( <p-1 \). The isomorphism \( \psi_s \) of Ogus's theorem [3, 8.20] gives the decomposition of \( X \), by a reduction of 2.1 for the truncated de Rham complex \( \tau_{\leqslant m} \), out of the isomorphism \( \varphi_{\widetilde{X}} \), where \( \widetilde{X} \) is the reduction of \( X^{\wedge} \) modulo \( p^2 \): if \( \varepsilon_m \) denotes the "gauge" \( i \mapsto \langle m-i \rangle \) [3, 8.18.3], the subcomplex \( (\Omega^{\bullet}_{X'/W})_{\varepsilon_r} \) of \( \Omega^{\bullet}_{X'/W} \), for \( r=m, m+1 \), is written \[ p^r \mathcal{O}_{X'} \to p^{r-1} \Omega^1_{X'/W} \to \ldots ; \] it is identified with \( R u_{X'/W*} \mathscr{J}^{[r]}_{/W} \); applying \( \psi_s \) to \( \varepsilon = \varepsilon_m, \varepsilon_{m+1} \), and passing to the quotient, one obtains the desired decomposition. It is this observation, implicit in Kato [14, proof of 2.6.1], that is at the origin of the present article.

If \( X \) has dimension \( N<p \), the isomorphism \( \psi_{s,N} \) moreover provides, for every integer \( n \geqslant 1 \), an analogue of the decomposition of 2.1 for the de Rham complex \( \Omega^{\bullet}_{X_n} \) of \( X_n / W_n(k) \), where \( X_n \) is the reduction of \( X^{\wedge} \) modulo \( p^n \). More precisely, denote by \( W_n X \) the scheme having the same underlying space as \( X \) and ringed by the sheaf \( W_n \mathcal{O}_X \) of Witt vectors of length \( n \) over \( \mathcal{O}_X \). The ring homomorphism \[ W_n \mathcal{O}_X \to \mathcal{O}_{X_n} , \qquad (a_0, \ldots, a_{n-1}) \mapsto \tilde{a}_0^{p^{n-1}} + p \tilde{a}_1^{p^{n-2}} + \ldots + p^{n-1} \tilde{a}_{n-1} , \] where \( \tilde{a}_i \) lifts \( a_i \), makes it possible to regard the components of \( \Omega^{\bullet}_{X_n} \) as modules over \( W_n X \). The Frobenius endomorphism of \( W_n \mathcal{O}_X \) defines a relative Frobenius morphism \( W_n X \to W_n X' \), which is a \( W_n(k) \)-morphism. The complex \( F_* \Omega^{\bullet}_{X_n} \) on \( W_n X' \) has linear differential. Let \( X'_n \) be deduced from \( X_n \) by the extension of scalars \( \sigma : W_n(k) \to W_n(k) \) (1.3), and denote by \( (\Omega^{\bullet}_{X_n}, pd) \) the complex deduced from the de Rham complex of \( X_n / W_n(k) \) by multiplication of the differential by \( p \). It is also a complex of modules, with linear differential, over \( W_n X' \). The construction of the isomorphism \( \psi_{s,N} \) gives, by reduction modulo \( p^n \), an isomorphism of \( D(W_n X') \):

\[ \tag{2.2.1} \varphi_{X'} : (\Omega^{\bullet}_{X_n}, pd) \xrightarrow{\sim} F_* \Omega^{\bullet}_{X_n} . \]

For \( n=1 \), \( X_1 = X \), \( (\Omega^{\bullet}_{X_n}, pd) = \bigoplus \Omega^i_{X/k}[-i] \) and (2.2.1) coincides with \( \varphi_{X_2} \). We refer to the articles of Fontaine-Messing [10] and Kato [14] for variants and applications of (2.2.1), in particular to the degeneration of the Hodge spectral sequence of \( X_n / W_n(k) \) for \( X \) proper over \( k \).

blocks.title: Corollary
blocks.html:
Corollary 2.3

With the notation of 2.1, let \( X \) be a smooth \( k \)-scheme of dimension \( \leqslant p \), liftable over \( W_2(k) \). Then the complex \( F_* \Omega^{\bullet}_{X/S} \) is isomorphic, in \( D(X') \), to a complex with zero differential.

The conclusion also means that \( F_* \Omega^{\bullet}_{X/S} \) is isomorphic, in \( D(X') \), to the sum of its \( \mathscr{H}^i[-i] \), or that there exists, in \( D(X') \), an isomorphism \[ \bigoplus \Omega^i_{X'/S}[-i] \xrightarrow{\sim} F_* \Omega^{\bullet}_{X/S} \] inducing \( C^{-1} \) on \( \mathscr{H}^i \) (cf. 3.1 below).

Proof▾

Let us prove 2.3. One reduces to assuming \( X \) connected. If \( \dim X<p \), it suffices to apply 2.1. So suppose that \( \dim X=p \). On \( X \), the locally free sheaves \( \Omega^i_{X/S} \) and \( \Omega^{p-i}_{X/S} \) are Serre-dual: the product \( \alpha \wedge \beta \) defines a perfect duality, with values in \( \Omega^p_{X/S} \), between \( \Omega^i_{X/S} \) and \( \Omega^{p-i}_{X/S} \). Since the morphism \( F=F_{X/S} \) is finite and flat, it follows, by Grothendieck duality, that \( F_* \Omega^i_{X/S} \) and \( F_* \Omega^{p-i}_{X/S} \) are again in duality (with values in \( \Omega^p_{X'/S} \)), given by the pairing \( (\alpha, \beta) \mapsto C(\alpha \wedge \beta) \), where one here denotes by \( C : F_* \Omega^p_{X/S} \to \Omega^p_{X'/S} \) the composite of \( F_* \Omega^p_{X/S} \to \mathscr{H}^p F_* \Omega^{\bullet}_{X/S} \) and the inverse of \( C^{-1} \) in degree \( p \) (1.2): the point is that \( C \) is none other than the trace morphism. It is moreover easy to check directly that this pairing is perfect. The transpose, for this duality, of the differential \( d \) of \( F_* \Omega^{\bullet}_{X/S} \) is again \( d \) (up to a sign depending on the conventions). This expresses that \[ C(d\alpha \wedge \beta) + C(\alpha \wedge d\beta) = C(d(\alpha \wedge \beta)) = 0 . \]

By 2.1, \( \tau_{<p} F_* \Omega^{\bullet}_{X/S} \) is isomorphic, in \( D(X') \), to the sum of its \( \mathscr{H}^i[-i] \). By duality, \( \tau_{\geqslant 1} F_* \Omega^{\bullet}_{X/S} \) has the same property. One has a distinguished triangle

\[ \tau_{<p} F_* \Omega^{\bullet}_{X/S} \to F_* \Omega^{\bullet}_{X/S} \to \mathscr{H}^p[-p] \xrightarrow{\ e\ } . \qquad (*) \]

Since \( \tau_{<p} F_* \Omega^{\bullet}_{X/S} \) is the sum of its \( \mathscr{H}^i[-i] \), the conclusion of 2.3 is equivalent to the vanishing of \[ e : \mathscr{H}^p[-p] \to \Big( \bigoplus_{i<p} \mathscr{H}^i[-i] \Big)[1] . \]

Let \( e_i \) (\( 0 \leqslant i \leqslant p-1 \)) be the components of \( e \): \[ e_i \in \Hom(\mathscr{H}^p[-p], \mathscr{H}^i[-i+1]) = H^{p-i+1}(X', \sHom(\mathscr{H}^p, \mathscr{H}^i)) . \]

The triangle (\(*\)) maps into the triangle \[ \tau_{[1,p-1]} F_* \Omega^{\bullet}_{X/S} \to \tau_{\geqslant 1} F_* \Omega^{\bullet}_{X/S} \to \mathscr{H}^p[-p] \to , \] where \( \tau_{[1,p-1]} = \tau_{\geqslant 1} \tau_{<p} = \tau_{<p} \tau_{\geqslant 1} \). Since \( \tau_{\geqslant 1} F_* \Omega^{\bullet}_{X/S} \) is the sum of its \( \mathscr{H}^i[-i] \), one therefore has \( e_i = 0 \) for \( i \neq 0 \). For \( i=0 \), the class \( e_i \) lives in \( H^{p+1}(X', \ldots) \), and this group is zero since \( \dim X=p \).

blocks.title: Corollary
blocks.html:
Corollary 2.4

With the notation of 2.1, let \( X \) be a proper smooth \( k \)-scheme of dimension \( \leqslant p \), liftable over \( W_2(k) \). Then the Hodge to de Rham spectral sequence

\[ \tag{2.4.1} E_1^{ij} = H^j(X, \Omega^i) \Rightarrow H^*_{DR}(X/k) \]

degenerates at \( E_1 \).

Proof▾

Since the \( H^j(X, \Omega^i) \) are finite-dimensional \( k \)-vector spaces, the conclusion means that one has, for every \( n \), \[ \sum_{i+j=n} \dim H^j(X, \Omega^i) = \dim H^n_{DR}(X/k) . \]

By 2.3, one has an isomorphism of \( D(X') \) \[ \bigoplus \Omega^i_{X'/S}[-i] \xrightarrow{\sim} F_* \Omega^{\bullet}_{X/S} . \]

One deduces from it, for every \( n \), an isomorphism \[ \bigoplus_i H^{n-i}(X', \Omega^i_{X'/S}) \xrightarrow{\sim} H^n(X', F_* \Omega^{\bullet}_{X/S}) . \]

Now, since \( F \) is finite, one has \( H^n(X', F_* \Omega^{\bullet}_{X/S}) = H^n(X, \Omega^{\bullet}_{X/S}) \). On the other hand, since \( X' \) is deduced from \( X \) by an extension of the field of scalars, one has \( \dim H^{n-i}(X', \Omega^i_{X'/S}) = \dim H^{n-i}(X, \Omega^i_{X/S}) \), whence the conclusion.

blocks.title: Corollary
blocks.html:
Corollary 2.5

With the notation of 2.1, let \( X \) be a proper smooth \( k \)-scheme liftable over \( W_2(k) \). Then the Hodge to de Rham spectral sequence satisfies \( E_1^{ij} = E_{\infty}^{ij} \) for \( i+j<p \).

Proof▾

The conclusion means that, for \( n<p \), one has \[ \sum_{i+j=n} \dim H^j(X, \Omega^i) = \dim H^n_{DR}(X/k) . \]

The short exact sequence of complexes \[ 0 \to \tau_{<p} F_* \Omega^{\bullet}_X \to F_* \Omega^{\bullet}_X \to F_* \Omega^{\bullet}_X / \tau_{<p} F_* \Omega^{\bullet}_X \to 0 \] yields, for \( n<p \), an isomorphism \[ H^n(X', \tau_{<p} F_* \Omega^{\bullet}_X) \xrightarrow{\sim} H^n(X', F_* \Omega^{\bullet}_X) = H^n_{DR}(X/k) . \]

Applying 2.2, one obtains, for \( n<p \), \[ \bigoplus_i H^{n-i}(X', \Omega^i_{X'}) \xrightarrow{\sim} H^n(X', F_* \Omega^{\bullet}_X) \] and one concludes as in 2.4.

See 4.1.4 for generalizations of 2.4 and 2.5.

blocks.title: Remarks
blocks.html:
Remarks 2.6

(i) Mumford [22] gave examples of smooth projective surfaces \( X/k \) possessing non-closed global 1-forms. Other examples were subsequently given by Lang [19], Raynaud and Szpiro [11]. These surfaces therefore do not lift over \( W_2(k) \). The same holds, for \( p=2 \), for the Enriques surfaces of type \( \alpha_2 \), for which the differential \( d_1 : H^1(\mathcal{O}) \to H^1(\Omega^1) \) is nonzero (cf. for example [13, II 7.3.8]). See also Suwa [26] for an interpretation of the degeneration condition of (2.4.1) at \( E_1 \) in terms of the structure of \( \Pic^{\tau}/\Pic^0 \) for surfaces such that \[ \chi(\mathcal{O}) - 1 + (b_1/2) = 0 . \]

(ii) Under the hypotheses of 2.4, it is not true in general that the Hodge symmetry \( h^{ij} = h^{ji} \) holds (where \( h^{ij} = \dim H^i(X, \Omega^j) \), cf. Serre [25, § 20]).

(iii) If \( X \) is a smooth \( k \)-scheme of dimension \( \geqslant p+1 \), liftable to a smooth scheme over \( W_2(k) \) (or even to a smooth formal scheme over \( W(k) \)), it is probably not true in general that \( F_* \Omega^{\bullet}_{X/k} \) is decomposable, in \( D(X') \), into its \( \mathscr{H}^i[-i] \). We do not, however, have a counterexample. We do not even know whether, for such \( X \), assumed moreover proper, the Hodge to de Rham spectral sequence degenerates at \( E_1 \).

(iv) If \( X \) is a smooth \( k \)-scheme, we will say that the complex \( F_* \Omega^{\bullet}_{X/k} \) is decomposable if it is the sum, in \( D(X') \), of its \( \mathscr{H}^i[-i] \) (cf. 3.1). If \( F_* \Omega^{\bullet}_{X/k} \) is decomposable, the same holds for \( F_* \Omega^{\bullet}_{Y/k} \) for \( Y \) étale over \( X \). If \( F_* \Omega^{\bullet}_{X/k} \) and \( F_* \Omega^{\bullet}_{Y/k} \) are decomposable, \( F_* \Omega^{\bullet}_{(X \times Y)/k} \) is so as well. If for every \( n \) the natural morphism \( \otimes^n \Omega^1_{X/k} \to \Omega^n_{X/k} \) admits a section, and \( X \) lifts over \( W_2(k) \), an argument analogous to that of 2.1 (a) shows again that \( F_* \Omega^{\bullet}_{X/k} \) is decomposable; this applies if \( X \) is an abelian variety over \( k \) (the decomposability of \( F_* \Omega^{\bullet}_{X/k} \) in this case was pointed out to us by M. Raynaud, with a different proof).

blocks.title: Corollary
blocks.html:
Corollary 2.7

Let \( K \) be a field of characteristic 0 and \( X \) a proper smooth \( K \)-scheme. Then the Hodge to de Rham spectral sequence

\[ \tag{2.7.1} E_1^{ij} = H^j(X, \Omega^i) \Rightarrow H^*_{DR}(X/K) \]

degenerates at \( E_1 \).

Proof▾

The conclusion also means that one has, for every \( n \),

\[ \sum_{i+j=n} h^{ij} = h^n , \qquad (*) \]

where \( h^{ij} = \dim H^j(X, \Omega^i) \) and \( h^n = \dim H^n_{DR}(X/K) \). One may assume \( X \) connected; let \( d \) be its dimension. Standard arguments show that there exist an integral ring \( A \) of finite type over \( \mathbf{Z} \), a proper smooth morphism \( f : \mathscr{X} \to \Spec(A) \), of relative dimension \( d \), and a homomorphism \( A \to K \) such that \( X = \mathscr{X} \otimes_A K \). The sheaves \( R^j f_* \Omega^i_{\mathscr{X}/A} \), \( R^n f_* \Omega^{\bullet}_{\mathscr{X}/A} \) are coherent, hence, after possibly replacing \( A \) by \( A[s^{-1}] \) for suitable \( s \in A \), one may assume that they are locally free (hence of formation compatible with any base change), and of constant ranks, \( h^{ij} \) and \( h^n \) respectively. Let \( T \) be the schematic closure, in \( \Spec(A) \), of a closed point of \( \Spec(A \otimes \mathbf{Q}) \); it is a scheme quasi-finite and flat over \( \Spec(\mathbf{Z}) \). Let us choose a closed point \( s \) of \( T \) at which \( T \) is étale and such that the characteristic \( p \) of the finite field \( k=k(s) \) is \( \geqslant d \). Let \( \mathcal{O}_s \) denote the local ring of \( T \) at \( s \), \( \mathfrak{m}_s \) its maximal ideal generated by \( p \), and \( \mathcal{O}_s / \mathfrak{m}_s^2 = W_2(k) \). The scheme \( \mathscr{X} \otimes_A (\mathcal{O}_s / \mathfrak{m}_s^2) \) is a smooth lifting of \( \mathscr{X}_s = \mathscr{X} \otimes_A k(s) \). Given the hypothesis made above, one has \( \dim_{k(s)} H^j(\mathscr{X}_s, \Omega^i) = h^{ij} \), and \( \dim_{k(s)} H^n_{DR}(\mathscr{X}_s/k(s)) = h^n \). But, since \( d \leqslant p \), the relation (\(*\)) is satisfied by 2.4.

blocks.title: Corollary
blocks.html:
Corollary 2.8 (Raynaud)

With the notation of 2.1, let \( X \) be a projective smooth \( k \)-scheme, purely of dimension \( d \), liftable over \( W_2(k) \), and let \( L \) be an invertible sheaf on \( X \). One makes one of the two following hypotheses:

(i) \( L \) is ample;

(ii) \( d=2 \) and \( L \) is numerically positive (i.e. one has \( L \cdot L>0 \) and \( L \cdot \mathcal{O}(D) \geqslant 0 \) for every effective divisor \( D \) on \( X \) ).

Then one has

\[ \tag{2.8.1} H^j(X, \Omega^i \otimes L) = 0 \quad \text{pour} \quad i+j>\sup(d, 2d-p) , \]
\[ \tag{2.8.2} H^j(X, \Omega^i \otimes L^{-1}) = 0 \quad \text{pour} \quad i+j<\inf(d, p) . \]

Note that (2.8.1) and (2.8.2) are equivalent by Serre duality. The heart of the proof is the following lemma:

blocks.title: Lemma
blocks.html:
Lemma 2.9

Let \( X \) be a smooth \( k \)-scheme, \( M \) an invertible sheaf on \( X \) and \( b \) an integer. Suppose that \( \tau_{<b} F_* \Omega^{\bullet}_X \) is isomorphic, in \( D(X') \), to a complex with zero differential, and that

\[ H^j(X, \Omega^i_X \otimes M^{\otimes p}) = 0 \quad \text{pour} \quad i+j<b . \qquad (*) \]

Then one has \[ H^j(X, \Omega^i_X \otimes M) = 0 \quad \text{pour} \quad i+j<b . \]

Proof▾

Let \( M' \) on \( X' \) be deduced from \( M \) by base change. One has \( F^* M' = M^{\otimes p} \), whence, by the projection formula, \[ H^j(X, M^{\otimes p} \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_X} \Omega^i_X) = H^j(X', M' \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_{X'}} F_* \Omega^i_X) \] for every \( (i,j) \). Since \( F_* \Omega^{\bullet}_X \) is a complex of \( \mathcal{O}_{X'} \)-modules (with \( \mathcal{O}_{X'} \)-linear differential), one can consider the tensor product \( M' \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_{X'}} F_* \Omega^{\bullet}_X \), and one has a spectral sequence \[ E_1^{ij} = H^j(X', M' \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_{X'}} F_* \Omega^i_X) \Rightarrow H^{i+j}(X', M' \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_{X'}} F_* \Omega^{\bullet}_X) . \]

The hypothesis (\(*\)) therefore implies that \( H^n(X', M' \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_{X'}} F_* \Omega^{\bullet}_X) = 0 \) for \( n<b \). But, for \( n<b \), one has \[ H^n(X', M' \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_{X'}} F_* \Omega^{\bullet}_X) = H^n(X', M' \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_{X'}} \tau_{<b} F_* \Omega^{\bullet}_X) . \]

Now one has, by hypothesis, an isomorphism of \( D(X') \) \[ \bigoplus_{i<b} \Omega^i_{X'}[-i] \xrightarrow{\sim} \tau_{<b} F_* \Omega^{\bullet}_X . \]

Consequently, for \( n<b \), one has \[ 0 = H^n(X', M' \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_{X'}} F_* \Omega^{\bullet}_X) = \bigoplus_i H^{n-i}(X', M' \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_{X'}} \Omega^i_{X'}) . \]

Since \( (X', M') \) is deduced from \( (X, M) \) by the base change \( F_s : S \xrightarrow{\sim} S \), one also has \[ H^{n-i}(X, M \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_X} \Omega^i_X) = 0 \] for \( n<b \) and every \( i \).

Proof of 2.8▾

Let us prove (2.8.2). By 2.1, for \( b \leqslant p \), \( \tau_{<b} F_* \Omega^{\bullet}_X \) is isomorphic, in \( D(X') \), to a complex with zero differential. Under hypothesis (i), one has \( H^j(X, \Omega^i_X \otimes L^{\otimes (-N)}) = 0 \) for \( N \) large enough and \( j<d \), in particular for \( N \) large enough and \( i+j<d \). Let \( M \) be the dual of \( L \). Applying 2.9 to the \( M^{\otimes p^n} \) and to \( b = \inf(p, d) \), one obtains (2.8.2) at the end of a descending induction on \( n \). Under hypothesis (ii), one again has \( H^j(X, \Omega^i_X \otimes L^{\otimes (-N)}) = 0 \) for \( N \) large enough and \( i+j<2 \). Indeed, it is trivial for \( i=j=0 \); for \( j=1, i=0 \), the assertion is due to Szpiro [21, Prop. 2]; finally, for \( j=0, i=1 \), it follows from the fact that, by Riemann-Roch, the dimension of \( H^0(X, L^{\otimes N}) \) tends to infinity as \( N \) tends to infinity. One then concludes as in case (i).

blocks.title: Remarks
blocks.html:
Remarks 2.10

(i) The idea of obtaining vanishing results by descending induction on Frobenius pullbacks is due to Szpiro (cf. [27, 28, 21]). Moreover, Esnault and Viehweg [7] have recently shown that, over \( \mathbf{C} \), there is a close link between the degeneration at \( E_1 \) of certain spectral sequences of "Hodge to de Rham" type and vanishing theorems of Kodaira type.

(ii) Raynaud [24] and Szpiro [9] have constructed examples of pairs \( (X, L) \), where \( X/k \) is a smooth projective surface and \( L \) an ample invertible sheaf on \( X \) such that \( H^1(X, L^{-1}) \neq 0 \). These surfaces therefore do not lift over \( W_2(k) \).

(iii) Let \( X \) be a smooth \( k \)-scheme. One will see in 3.6 that if \( X \) does not lift over \( W_2(k) \), then \( \tau_{\leqslant 1} F_* \Omega^{\bullet}_{X/k} \) is not isomorphic, in \( D(X') \), to a complex with zero differential. This "pathology" may be invisible at the level of the Hodge spectral sequence or of vanishing statements of Kodaira type: for \( p \geqslant 7 \), Raynaud is able to construct, by the Godeaux-Serre method [25], a surface \( X \) smooth and projective over \( \mathbf{F}_p \), not lifting over \( \mathbf{Z}/p^2 \), and such that: a) the Hodge to de Rham spectral sequence of \( X \) degenerates at \( E_1 \); b) every ample invertible sheaf on \( X \) satisfies the Kodaira-Akizuki-Nakano vanishing theorem.

blocks.title: Corollary
blocks.html:
Corollary 2.11 (Kodaira-Akizuki-Nakano [1, 18], Ramanujam [23])

Let \( K \) be a field of characteristic 0 and \( X \) a projective smooth \( K \)-scheme, purely of dimension \( d \), and \( L \) an invertible sheaf on \( X \). One assumes that \( L \) is ample, or that \( d=2 \) and that \( L \) is numerically positive. Then one has \[ H^j(X, \Omega^i \otimes L) = 0 \quad \text{pour} \quad i+j>d \] (or, what amounts to the same thing, by Serre duality, \( H^j(X, \Omega^i \otimes L^{-1}) = 0 \) for \( i+j<d \) ).

Proof▾

One deduces 2.11 from 2.8 as one deduced 2.6 from 2.1; we will omit the details (for the numerically positive case, cf. [21, p. 42]).

blocks.title: Corollary
blocks.html:
Corollary 2.12 ("weak Lefschetz", cf. Berthelot [2])

With the notation of 2.1, let \( X \) be a projective smooth \( k \)-scheme purely of dimension \( d \), and \( D \subset X \) a smooth divisor. One assumes \( X \) and \( D \) liftable over \( W_2(k) \) and \( D \) ample. Then the restriction arrow \( H^n_{DR}(X/k) \to H^n_{DR}(D/k) \) is an isomorphism for \( n<\inf(p, d) - 1 \) and an injection for \( n=\inf(p, d) - 1 \).

Proof▾

The kernel \( \Omega^{\bullet}_X(\log D)(-D) \) of \( \Omega^{\bullet}_X \to \Omega^{\bullet}_D \) [cf. 4.2.2(c)] admits a dévissage ("weight filtration") \[ 0 \to \Omega^{\bullet}_X(-D) \to \Omega^{\bullet}_X(\log D)(-D) \to \Omega^{\bullet-1}_D(-D) \to 0 . \]

The conclusion of 2.12 means that \[ H^n(X, \Omega^{\bullet}_X(\log D)(-D)) = 0 \quad \text{pour} \quad n<\inf(p, d) . \]

One applies 2.8 to \( (X, \mathcal{O}_X(D)) \) and \( (D, \mathcal{O}_D(D)) \).
